title: 8-bit Quantization Provides No Privacy Benefit Against Training-Free Embedding Inversion

contributions.purpose: Enable a fair comparison of quantization's privacy benefit by controlling for confounding retrieval-utility differences.
contributions.mechanism: Calibrate a Gaussian noise baseline to match 8-bit quantization's retrieval utility, then attack both with ZSInvert, a training-free LLM-based embedding inversion.
contributions.evaluation: Utility-matched protocol anchored at nDCG@10 approximately 0.544 for both defenses.
contributions.source_quote: The first utility-matched evaluation of embedding quantization against training-free inversion attacks, enabling fair comparison of privacy benefits.

contributions.purpose: Determine whether 8-bit quantization actually protects embeddings from inversion.
contributions.mechanism: Measure attribute recovery (Canary-EM) under quantization versus utility-matched Gaussian noise using ZSInvert.
contributions.evaluation: Negative result: quantization gives only 6% relative reduction in attribute recovery (Canary-EM 6.0% vs 6.4%) versus 70% reduction for noise (down to 1.9%).
contributions.source_quote: A surprising negative result: 8-bit quantization provides negligible privacy protection (6% reduction) while utility-matched noise achieves 70% reduction.

contributions.purpose: Explain mechanistically why quantization fails to protect while noise succeeds.
contributions.mechanism: Geometric analysis of how each defense perturbs cosine-similarity structure and angular deviation that ZSInvert exploits.
contributions.evaluation: Quantization preserves structure (0.9 degree angular deviation, pairwise rho=0.9999); noise disrupts it (41.5 degree deviation, rho=0.656).
contributions.source_quote: A geometric explanation: quantization preserves cosine similarity structure (rho=0.9999) that attacks exploit, while noise disrupts it (rho=0.656).

contributions.purpose: Guide practitioners on relying on efficiency optimizations for privacy.
contributions.mechanism: Argue from the results that efficiency optimizations and privacy defenses require separate, explicit mechanisms.
contributions.evaluation: No separate experiment; implication drawn from the negative and geometric results above.
contributions.source_quote: A practical implication: efficiency optimizations and privacy defenses require separate, explicit mechanisms; practitioners should not rely on quantization for privacy.

self_declared_provenance.quote: We present the first utility-matched evaluation of 8-bit quantization against ZSInvert, a training-free inversion attack.

Our work addresses this gap by providing the first utility-matched evaluation of quantization against training-free inversion attacks, enabling fair comparison of privacy benefits across defense mechanisms.

notes: NEGATIVE-RESULT paper: central claim is that 8-bit quantization provides no meaningful privacy benefit (6% vs 70% for utility-matched noise). Quantization vs noise is effectively a tie on attribute recovery (Canary-EM 6.0% vs 6.4%). Uses ZSInvert (Zhang et al. 2025) as the attack rather than proposing a new attack.
